result.title: Benchmarking Quantum Kernel SVMs for Credit Card Fraud Detection: Performance Realities Under NISQ Constraints
result.summary: Detecting credit card fraud is notoriously difficult because fraudulent charges make up less than 0.2% of total transactions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML), particularly Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machines (QSVM), promises richer feature representations by embedding classical data into high-dimensional Hilbert spaces. However, whether this theoretical advantage holds up when managing real-world financial data bottlenecks remains unclear. We designed a controlled benchmark comparing three quantum encodings, Angle, ZZFeatureMap, and IQP against classical models while keeping sample sizes, feature counts, and scaling strictly matched. To handle class skew without corrupting quantum state overlaps, we embedded synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) directly into the quantum Gram matrix workflow, raising PR-AUC scores by roughly +0.04 across feature maps. When trained on the full European credit card dataset with 30 features, classical baselines reached a top PR-AUC of 0.983. However, restricting classical models to match QSVM hardware constraints (500 samples, 4 PCA features) dropped their PR-AUC to 0.750. This puts our best quantum result 0.730 PR-AUC using IQP encoding on 150 samples into realistic context. Testing on physical quantum hardware reduced performance further to 0.62 due to CNOT gate errors and thermal noise. Overall, our findings pinpoint two main operational bottlenecks for near-term quantum kernels: the scaling of Gram matrix evaluation and heavy information loss from squeezing features onto small qubit registers.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在高度类别不平衡的信用卡欺诈检测任务上，对 Angle、ZZFeatureMap、IQP 三种量子编码的量子核 SVM 与严格对齐样本量、特征数的经典基线做受控基准比较，并将 SMOTE 直接嵌入量子 Gram 矩阵流程，最后在真实量子硬件上测试噪声与门错误带来的性能下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 量子核 Gram 矩阵实质是在高维嵌入空间中对样本做相似性度量，论文指出把特征压缩到小量子寄存器会带来严重信息损失，这一「编码方式决定相似性几何、压缩导致信息坍缩」的观察可能与 LVR 中 latent 表示相似度的内容依赖与压缩代价分析形成类比，可供核查；但其任务与视觉多模态推理无直接联系，迁移属推测。
